🟡📝 **Consider · docs: Check reads a possibly stale `origin/main`, so 'the day main takes the number' depends on a fetch**

`mainNames()` runs `git ls-tree origin/main`, which reads the local remote-tracking ref. `git push` does not update that ref. Only `git fetch` or `git pull` does. A developer who has not fetched since `main` took a number will still pass the pre-push hook. The header (lines 9–10) says the collision is flagged "the day `main` takes the number", and `webcam-track.md:134-136` says it "shows up the day it happens". Both claims hold only after a fetch. Either say so in both places, or run a quiet `git fetch origin main` first (ignoring failures, as you already do for a missing ref) so the check matches what the docs promise.

🟡📝 **Consider · docs: "seven stacked PRs, one per layer" lists six layers**

The sentence says seven stacked PRs, one per layer, but it names six layers: recorder, vault, scene, preview, export, protection. The table above it shows that the seventh PR, #437, was the design PR (spec and ADRs), not a layer. Suggested wording: "a design PR, then six stacked PRs, one per layer", or name #437 as the design PR.

#454 is still open (its base was retargeted to `main`, but it has not merged), and `wc2` does not exist on `origin/main` yet. Listing it under **What shipped** says the lane filmstrip and the `wc2` export-reuse revision are live when they are not. The banner gets this right; the table, the `wc2` mention at line 83 and "the webcam lane had no thumbnails (#454)" at line 85 read as already fixed.

Consider marking the row as open (e.g. `#454 (open)`), or moving it under follow-ups until it merges.

This lists six layers, and the table has six implementation PRs (#441–#446). "Seven" only works if you count the design PR #437, which the sentence has already covered as "one spec and two ADRs".

```suggestion
  one assumption nobody had verified (protection from creation), then six stacked PRs, one
  per layer: recorder, vault, scene, preview, export, protection.
```

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Opus 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**

Fixed in 53414371: the check now runs a quiet `git fetch origin main` (10 s timeout) before comparing, and falls back to the ref it has when offline, so the header and the doc's claim hold.
